---
title: "Demo: Information Leakage"
subtitle: "FW 532 · R version"
---

Setup.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(terra)    # rasters (gridded maps)
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)     # ROC curves and AUC
library(ape)      # Moran's I
library(here)     # file paths relative to the project folder

envStack <- rast(here("data", "envStack.tif"))
```

Generate a new raster variable which is precipitation seasonality plus noise in the south (highly correlated) and random noise in the north. The north/south boundary is latitude 45.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4
noiseRast <- envStack$Precipitation.Seasonality
set.seed(2023)
noiseRast <- setValues(noiseRast, rnorm(n = ncell(noiseRast)))
noiseRast <- mask(noiseRast, mask = envStack$Precipitation.Seasonality)
simRast <- envStack$Precipitation.Seasonality + noiseRast

northExt <- ext(xmin(envStack), xmax(envStack), 45, ymax(envStack))
southExt <- ext(xmin(envStack), xmax(envStack), ymin(envStack), 45)
northRast <- crop(simRast, northExt) - crop(envStack$Precipitation.Seasonality, northExt) # = just the noise
southRast <- crop(simRast, southExt)
newVar <- merge(northRast, southRast)
newStack <- c(envStack$Precipitation.Seasonality, newVar)
names(newStack) <- c("Precipitation.Seasonality", "simRast")
plot(newStack)
```

Sample data from the south. Generate a species that responds to precipitation seasonality.

```{r}
logistic <- function(x) { 1 / (1 + exp(-x)) }

# get points
nPoints <- 1000
#nPoints = 3000
set.seed(1234)
simPts <- spatSample(southRast, size = nPoints, method = "random",
                     na.rm = TRUE, xy = TRUE)
latLongs <- simPts[, c("x", "y")]

# scale the climate variables:
scaledEnv <- extract(newStack, latLongs, ID = FALSE)
scaledEnv[, 1:2] <- apply(scaledEnv[, 1:2], 2, scale)

# set parameters
intercept <- -1.5
beta1 <- -1.5
pOccRaster <- logistic(intercept +
                         beta1 * scale(newStack$Precipitation.Seasonality))
names(pOccRaster) <- "pOcc"

# get the values that correspond to the points we selected:
pOccs <- extract(pOccRaster, latLongs, ID = FALSE)$pOcc

# sample from these probabilities (a *different* seed for a different random step; see Lab 1):
set.seed(5678)
presAbs <- rbinom(n = nPoints, size = 1, prob = pOccs)

# put response and variables together in a data.frame:
modelingDF <- data.frame(presAbs, scaledEnv, latLongs)

# plot the result
plot(pOccRaster)
points(modelingDF$x[modelingDF$presAbs == 0], modelingDF$y[modelingDF$presAbs == 0], col = "blue", pch = 20)
points(modelingDF$x[modelingDF$presAbs == 1], modelingDF$y[modelingDF$presAbs == 1], col = "red", pch = 20)
```

Split these data randomly in half for training and testing. Fit a model to the WRONG variable - the simulated raster that is correlated with precipitation seasonality in the south.

```{r}
trainData <- modelingDF[1:floor(nPoints/2), ]
testData <- modelingDF[(floor(nPoints/2) + 1):nPoints, ]

modelNew <- glm(formula = presAbs ~ simRast,
                data = trainData,
                family = "binomial")

modelNew
```

Predict on the randomly withheld (southern) test data.

```{r}
predProbs <- predict(modelNew,
                     testData,
                     type = "response")

resids <- abs(predProbs - testData$presAbs)
p <- ggplot(data = data.frame(resids, x = testData$x, y = testData$y),
            mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, col = resids)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_continuous(low = "white", high = "red") +
  coord_quickmap()
p
```

Test residuals for spatial autocorrelation - reject the null that there is none.

```{r}
resid.dists <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(testData$x, testData$y))) # distances in degrees of longitude/latitude
resid.dists.inv <- 1/resid.dists
diag(resid.dists.inv) <- 0
Moran.I(resids, resid.dists.inv)
```

Look at ROC on the random test holdout.

```{r}
# create an ROC object for these data:
ROCcurve <- roc(response = testData$presAbs, predictor = predProbs)
plot(ROCcurve) # plot it
plot(smooth(ROCcurve), add = TRUE, col = "blue") # add a smoothed version
# make a confidence interval object for the curve (by bootstrapping, so set a seed):
set.seed(1111)
curveCI <- ci(ROCcurve, of = "thresholds")
plot(curveCI, col = "grey") # plot it with grey error bars
```

```{r}
auc(ROCcurve) # get the area under the curve
ci(ROCcurve) # get a confidence interval for the AUC
```

Now sample some points in the north, where the variables are NOT correlated.

```{r}
set.seed(4321)
newPts <- spatSample(northRast, size = nPoints, method = "random",
                     na.rm = TRUE, xy = TRUE)
latLongs <- newPts[, c("x", "y")]

# scale the climate variables:
scaledEnv <- extract(newStack, latLongs, ID = FALSE)
scaledEnv[, 1:2] <- apply(scaledEnv[, 1:2], 2, scale)

# set parameters
intercept <- -1.5
beta1 <- -1.5
pOccRaster <- logistic(intercept +
                         beta1 * scale(newStack$Precipitation.Seasonality))
names(pOccRaster) <- "pOcc"

# get the values that correspond to the points we selected:
pOccs <- extract(pOccRaster, latLongs, ID = FALSE)$pOcc

# sample from these probabilities:
set.seed(8765)
presAbs <- rbinom(n = nPoints, size = 1, prob = pOccs)

# put response and variables together in a data.frame:
modelingDF <- data.frame(presAbs, scaledEnv, latLongs)

# plot the result
plot(pOccRaster)
points(modelingDF$x[modelingDF$presAbs == 0], modelingDF$y[modelingDF$presAbs == 0], col = "blue", pch = 20)
points(modelingDF$x[modelingDF$presAbs == 1], modelingDF$y[modelingDF$presAbs == 1], col = "red", pch = 20)
```

Predict values in the north based on the model fit in the south.

```{r}
newPreds <- predict(modelNew,
                    modelingDF,
                    type = "response")
ROCcurveNEW <- roc(response = modelingDF$presAbs, predictor = newPreds)
plot(ROCcurveNEW) # plot it
plot(smooth(ROCcurveNEW), add = TRUE, col = "blue") # add a smoothed version
# make a confidence interval object for the curve:
set.seed(2222)
curveCINEW <- ci(ROCcurveNEW, of = "thresholds")
plot(curveCINEW, col = "grey") # plot it with grey error bars
auc(ROCcurveNEW) # get the area under the curve
ci(ROCcurveNEW) # get a confidence interval for the AUC
```

Compare the curves.

```{r}
plot(ROCcurve) # plot it
plot(ROCcurveNEW, add = TRUE, col = "red")
legend("bottomright", c("South: rand. holdout", "North: independent/new data"),
       col = c("black", "red"), lty = c(1, 1), lwd = c(2, 2))
```

So we have identified a case where a model looked decent on holdout data but transferred very poorly to a new location. But it was a contrived example, and I don't think that blockCV or similar would have detected the problem. How can we make this example 1) more realistic, and 2) something that can be addressed with a smarter approach to model evaluation???
